Usage: rulebearing fmt [OPTIONS] <RESULT-JSON>

Arguments:
  <RESULT-JSON>

          azure-devops, github-annotations, agent, baseline, sarif, junit, trx, dot, ddot, archi,
          cdot, flat, fdot, x-dot-webpage, mermaid, d2, metrics, html, markdown, anon, null)
          
          [default: err]

  -f, --output-to <FILE>
          File to write output to; - for stdout
          
          [default: -]

  -I, --include-only <REGEX>
          Only include modules matching the regex

  -F, --focus <REGEX>
          Only include modules matching the regex and their neighbours

      --focus-depth <NUMBER>
          The depth to focus on

  -R, --reaches <REGEX>
          Only include modules matching the regex and every module that reaches them

  -H, --highlight <REGEX>
          Mark modules matching the regex as highlighted

  -x, --exclude <REGEX>
          Exclude all modules matching the regex

  -S, --collapse <REGEX-OR-DEPTH>
          Collapse modules to a folder depth (a single digit) or to the first match of a regex

      --ignore-known [<FILE>]
          Ignore the known violations saved in FILE, in place of options.knownViolations (default:
          .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json)

      --no-ignore-known
          Apply no known violations, options.knownViolations included: every finding at its rule's
          severity

  -e, --exit-code
          Exit with the number of error violations

      --exit-code-mode <MODE>
          With --exit-code: default (the count) or strict (10 + the count, so 2 and 3 are never a
          count)

          Possible values:
          - default: The error count, capped at 255, as dependency-cruiser exits
          - strict:  10 plus the error count when there is one, capped at 255, so 2 and 3 only
